approach: Add one reading-acceptance check, `check_scope_limit` in crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs, as a single `step!(check_scope_limit(reading));` line in `refusing_check` after `check_defined_terms` and before `check_boundary_and_repo_files`. Root cause: nothing at the reading gate compares a scope limit with the files Athena always writes (CHANGELOG.md, forced by `ensure_changelog`, reading.rs:297, run before the gate at reading.rs:859) or with the readers of a changed config. A limit written from the named files therefore passes the gate and fails at verification (class scope-criterion-too-narrow-misses-dependent-tests; jobs 20261018-045437-7z81 and 20261023-052543-9bw7). A scope limit is a criterion for which `athena_context::briefs::limits_changed_files` (briefs.rs:146) is true, the same matcher that builds the allowlist at verification (`allowed_paths`, briefs.rs:115). The check runs for capability `change` readings with no question and does two mechanical things, with no scan of repo contents. (1) CHANGELOG half: a limiting criterion is refused unless it names CHANGELOG.md without forbidding it, points to 'the deliverables', or is a bare form with no exception word. A name next to a negation word ('CHANGELOG.md is not changed', 'CHANGELOG.md stays as it is') is refused (round 3, finding 5). (2) Config half: when a limit exists and athena.toml or defaults.toml is a deliverable, the reading needs a `Consumers:` assumption. It must (a) name one or more path-like words, none of them the config file itself, and every one a deliverable (or under a deliverable ending in '/'); or (b) say 'unchanged' or 'no change'; or (c) say 'none found'. Path-like means a word with '/' or ending .rs/.toml/.md/.json/.yml/.yaml, so xtask/ readers count (round 3, finding 3). Support work: one READING_RULES line, unit tests in reading.rs, corpus cases with new input-form tags, a one-constant fixture fix in run/tests.rs (forced), a steward test showing stored proposals leave the queue, a replay step with a stop rule, a CHANGELOG entry and decision D166.

decisions.choice: CHANGELOG half applies to every criterion for which `limits_changed_files` is true. It is exempt only when the lowercased text names `changelog.md` (a name from the default-written table) with no negation word within 3 words either side, or contains 'deliverable', or is bare (none of the whole words only, outside, except, beyond, besides, apart, aside, than; hyphens split words as in the matcher). A CHANGELOG.md deliverable alone does not repair the limit text. Negation words: not, never, unchanged, untouched, unmodified, excluding, excluded, without, stays, stay, kept, keep, remains, remain. 'no' and 'except' are left out on purpose, because 'No file outside README.md and CHANGELOG.md changed' and 'except CHANGELOG.md' are valid.
decisions.reason: `build_reading` calls `ensure_changelog` before `check_reading_acceptance`, so every change reading already lists CHANGELOG.md at the gate; a rule that accepted 'CHANGELOG.md listed' would never fire. The 9bw7 failure was a limit sentence that forbids the forced edit. 'test-only change' and 'only the docs may change' forbid it just as much, so the rule does not wait for a named file. The negation window (round 3, finding 5) closes the case where a limit mentions CHANGELOG.md only to exclude it, which is the very failure the check exists to stop. A bare 'No other file is changed' lists no exception and stays accepted. The window is a word list and can miss other phrasings; D166 says so.

rejected.option: Accept when CHANGELOG.md is a deliverable (the literal reading of criterion 2)
rejected.why: Inert for every production reading, so the class stays open.

rejected.option: Fire only when the limit names a file (round 1 design)
rejected.why: Leaves 'test-only change' and 'only the docs may change' accepted although the job must still edit CHANGELOG.md.

rejected.option: Refuse a limit unless it lists every deliverable by name
rejected.why: Larger refusal rate than the evidence supports; 'the deliverables' is the existing way to point at the list.

rejected.option: Make `ensure_changelog` append CHANGELOG.md to a limiting criterion's text or allowed list instead of refusing (finding 7)
rejected.why: It would fix the 9bw7 shape with no new refusals, but it rewrites the reader's criterion silently, so the reader never learns that a limit must account for default-written files, and the config-consumer half would still need a refusal. The accepted reading chose refuse-and-repair before a producer runs, and that stays the design.

rejected.option: Treat any mention of changelog.md as the exemption (round 2 design)
rejected.why: A limit such as 'CHANGELOG.md is not changed' would pass although it forbids the forced edit.

decisions.choice: Only criteria are scanned; out_of_scope items are not. The matcher is `limits_changed_files` imported from athena_context::briefs; exception-word and negation tests are small private helpers sharing one word tokenizer (lowercase, hyphen to space, trim non-alphanumeric ends).
decisions.reason: One definition for the gate and for verification-time enforcement (`limiting_criterion` reads criteria only, briefs.rs:103-108), so the gate cannot drift from what is enforced. out_of_scope items are exclusions, never an allowlist, and 'files kept from job X' would cause false refusals. This departs from the reading's 'criterion or out_of_scope item'; raised as a User question.

rejected.option: A new phrase list ('only', 'nothing else', 'no other') as the trigger in checks.rs
rejected.why: A second matcher that would drift from `limits_changed_files`.

rejected.option: Also scan out_of_scope items
rejected.why: Enforcement ignores them, and exclusions would cause false refusals.

decisions.choice: The config half fires only with a limiting criterion (exempt or not) and a deliverable whose normalized path is athena.toml or defaults.toml. It is met only by a `Consumers:` assumption (trimmed, case-insensitive prefix, like `code_surveys` in surveys.rs:116) in one of three forms: (a) it names at least one path-like word other than the config file itself, and every path-like word is a deliverable path or lies under a deliverable ending in '/'; (b) the line says 'unchanged' or 'no change'; (c) the line says 'none found'. A Consumers line with no such path and neither phrase is refused. Path-like = contains '/' or ends in .rs, .toml, .md, .json, .yml or .yaml, after trimming quotes, backticks, brackets, a leading './' and end punctuation. `names_crates_path` is no longer reused.
decisions.reason: With a limit the deliverable list is the allowlist (briefs.rs:110-126). In 7z81 the tests that load the real athena.toml were not deliverables, so the scope guard failed the job; the introspection's prevention was that the reading should then allow those files. Requiring every named consumer to be a deliverable does that. Round 3, finding 3: athena.toml is also read outside crates/ (xtask/tests/policy.rs, xtask/src/main.rs), so the parser checks every path-like word, not only crates/ words, and an xtask path that is a deliverable now satisfies the rule. This is a revised sense of criterion 3's 'either': a bare crates/ test deliverable no longer satisfies it, because that left 7z81's failure open. Raised as a User question and recorded in D166.

rejected.option: Accept any crates/ test deliverable as the answer (round 1; the literal criterion 3)
rejected.why: An unrelated test deliverable such as refusal_corpus.rs satisfied the rule without any search and without widening the allowlist to the real consumers.

rejected.option: Accept a Consumers line naming paths that are not deliverables
rejected.why: The producer would have to edit them and the scope guard would fail the job as in 7z81.

rejected.option: Only check words containing crates/ (round 2)
rejected.why: An xtask/ consumer that is not a deliverable would pass, and one that is a deliverable would be refused.

rejected.option: Scan repo content for files that load the config
rejected.why: Out of scope; readers see a plain copy and the gate must stay deterministic.

rejected.option: Require the consumer rule for every config deliverable, even without a limit
rejected.why: Without a limit the producer may touch consumers freely; it would refuse readings that cannot suffer the failure.

decisions.choice: Default-written files go in a const table `DEFAULT_WRITTEN_FILES: [(&str, &str); 1]` whose only row is (`super::CHANGELOG_PATH`, reason text), and config files in `CONFIG_FILES: [&str; 2]`, both in checks.rs.
decisions.reason: `CHANGELOG_PATH` (reading.rs:293) is the constant `ensure_changelog` writes; checks.rs is a child module of reading with `use super::*` (checks.rs:3), so the gate and the writer share one source. The table follows GOVERNANCE_BY_DELIVERABLE; the reason text feeds the error; a future default file is one row.

rejected.option: Hard-code the string CHANGELOG.md in the logic
rejected.why: Can drift from what ensure_changelog writes and loses the reason text.

The text matches `limits_changed_files`, has 'outside' and omits CHANGELOG.md, so the new check refuses it and the scope tests fail; the edit is forced by the rule. The file is under crates/, the scope the request gave; it is listed in `files` and raised as a User question so the deliverable list can include it.

rejected.why: A test-shaped hole; the class would stay open for single-file limits.

decisions.choice: Add one steward test in crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs (tests module, next to `a_proposed_request_with_a_passing_stored_reading_is_listed_read`, line 2330): `a_proposed_request_whose_stored_limit_omits_changelog_leaves_the_queue`. Build the stored reading with `stored_reading(1, "b", "src/a.rs")` and set its criterion to 'Only src/a.rs may change'; assert `queued_work` is empty. A control with 'Only src/a.rs and CHANGELOG.md may change' stays listed with `read` true. State the effect in D166 and the CHANGELOG entry: Proposed jobs whose latest stored reading carries such a limit leave the drain queue (`queued_work`, steward.rs:416-425) until they are read again (finding 6).
decisions.reason: `queued_work` re-checks every Proposed job's stored reading with `check_reading_text`, so the new refusal reaches stored readings silently. A test with a real stored limit reading shows it; the control guards against the test passing for another reason. Test-only edit.

rejected.option: Cover it only with the whole-crate test run
rejected.why: No existing steward test stores a limit reading, so nothing would show the effect.

decisions.choice: Add an in-loop replay step with a stop rule (finding 4). After the suite passes, the producer reads the replay result the loop gives it (the loop replays past readings through `check_reading_text` when crates/ changes: `touches_reading_rules`, replay.rs:314; limit `replay_limit_percent`, replay.rs:304) and may run `athena check-reading` on any stored reading fixtures. If the newly refused share is above 8% (declared 3% plus REPLAY_DECLARED_MARGIN_POINTS = 5, replay.rs:161, 296-308), the producer stops and reports the measured share. It does not narrow the check or edit the declared figure.
decisions.reason: Round 2 widened the trigger, so the 3% estimate may be low; the hold at verification is `newly * 100 > total * 8`. Stopping gives the user the measurement, and the declared figure stays an honest estimate.

rejected.option: Narrow the check or raise the declared share until the replay passes
rejected.why: Tunes the rule to the corpus; the user decides on a measured number.

rejected.option: Leave measurement to verification only
rejected.why: The producer's loop already runs the same replay and can report early.

risks.risk: False refusals: `limits_changed_files` matches a criterion that mentions a limit in passing, and the broader CHANGELOG half refuses such limits too.
risks.mitigation: The matcher already errs toward not matching (briefs.rs:140-145). The repair is one phrase ('and CHANGELOG.md' or 'the deliverables'), given in the error text. Bare forms stay accepted and are pinned by corpus Accept cases. Step 10 reads the replay and stops above 8%.

risks.risk: The Consumers rule cannot verify that the search was done; 'none found' can be written without searching.
risks.mitigation: D166 states the limit: the gate forces the question and checks that every named consumer is a deliverable; scanning repo content is out of scope. A consumer the reader does not name is the remaining gap and is named in D166. The negation and exception word lists are fixed lists and can miss other phrasings; the same note applies.

risks.risk: The negation window refuses a valid limit or misses a negation phrased otherwise.
risks.mitigation: The window is 3 words and the word list excludes 'no' and 'except'; unit and corpus cases pin 'is not changed', 'stays as it is' (Refuse) and 'No file outside X and CHANGELOG.md changed' and 'CHANGELOG.md may change; src not changed' (Accept). Repair text names the fix.

risks.risk: The new READING_RULES line pushes a rule line past 220 bytes or the section past its bound.
risks.mitigation: Keep the line to about 200 bytes; if the section exceeds the bound, set the bound to the measured size plus a small margin and fix its comment. `cargo test -p athena-context` shows it. The reader prompt is untouched.

risks.risk: Another test or fake reader outside the places found pushes a limit phrase through the gate and starts failing.
risks.mitigation: Step 11 runs `cargo test --locked` for the whole workspace. A failing fixture gets 'and CHANGELOG.md' in its limit text, as LIMIT does; the check is not weakened.

risks.risk: run/tests.rs and steward.rs are not among the six listed deliverables, so a scope guard built from this job's deliverable list could flag them.
risks.mitigation: Both edits are small, listed in `files`, raised as a User question and checked by `git diff --stat`. Exempting README.md-only limits in the check was rejected as a hole in the rule.

risks.risk: A Consumers line with a `./` prefix, quotes or backticks, or a prose word, is mis-parsed and refused.
risks.mitigation: Trim quotes, backticks, brackets, './' and end punctuation as `allowed_paths` does (briefs.rs:119-120); a deliverable ending in '/' covers paths under it; unit and corpus cases pin both forms. A word like 'e.g.' is not path-like (no '/', no listed extension).

risks.risk: The replay share exceeds 8% and holds the job.
risks.mitigation: Step 10 stops and reports the measured share; the producer does not narrow the check or edit the declared figure. The producer snapshot has no records/, so the replay may only be visible in the loop's output; if it is not visible, the producer says so in its output.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `scope_limit_changelog` calls `refusing_check` through the existing `gate_refuser` helper (reading.rs:6977) on readings built by `governed_reading` (reading.rs:4329; capability change, no question). Refused with Some("check_scope_limit"): 'Only docs/x.md may change' with no CHANGELOG.md deliverable; the same with a CHANGELOG.md deliverable but a limit that omits it (production shape after `ensure_changelog`); 'test-only change'; 'only the docs may change'; 'Only docs/x.md may change; CHANGELOG.md is not changed'; 'Only docs/x.md may change and CHANGELOG.md stays as it is'. Accepted (None): 'Only docs/x.md and CHANGELOG.md may change' with the CHANGELOG.md deliverable; 'Only docs/x.md and CHANGELOG.md may change; src not changed' (negation farther than 3 words); 'No file outside docs/x.md and CHANGELOG.md changed'; 'Only the deliverables may change'; bare 'No other file is changed'; 'production unchanged'; the same limits as an out_of_scope item or on a reading with a question or capability other than change. 'With CHANGELOG.md listed' in criterion 2 is shown as CHANGELOG.md named in the limit text (the deliverable alone would be inert in production; open question). A second test asserts `check_reading_acceptance` returns Err whose text names CHANGELOG.md and its reason.
demonstrations.observes: The first reading is refused under the name check_scope_limit; the repaired and bare readings return None.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the step line `refusing_check` returns None for the first reading, so the Some("check_scope_limit") assertion fails; a rule that accepted a CHANGELOG.md deliverable alone, fired only on named files, or exempted a negated name would fail the production-shaped, 'test-only change' and 'is not changed' assertions.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `refusing_check` and `check_reading_acceptance` (checks.rs:515, :487). Fixture: an in-memory `Reading` from `governed_reading`/`scoped_reading` (reading.rs:4329, 3473) passed as an argument; no double. The seam exists today; steps 2-3 add the check and step 8 the tests.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `scope_limit_config_consumers` builds `governed_reading(&["athena.toml", "docs/x.md"], &["Only athena.toml, docs/x.md and CHANGELOG.md may change"], &[])` (the limit names CHANGELOG.md so only the config half fires; athena.toml is named so `check_governance_coverage` passes). Mapping of criterion 3's 'neither a crates/ test deliverable nor a Consumers: assumption ... adding either makes it pass' to the revised rule: 'adding the test deliverable' stands for adding the consumer as a deliverable AND naming it in a Consumers line; 'adding the Consumers assumption' stands for a line that says unchanged, none found, or names only deliverables. Refused (check_scope_limit, error names athena.toml and `Consumers:`): the base reading; the base plus an unrelated crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs deliverable and no Consumers line (the revised sense, see open questions); `Consumers: crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs loads athena.toml` when that path is not a deliverable; `Consumers: crates/a.rs (deliverable), xtask/tests/policy.rs` when the xtask path is not a deliverable; a Consumers line with no path and no phrase; a Consumers line naming only athena.toml. Accepted (None): the same Consumers line with crates/athena-cli/tests/common/mod.rs added as a deliverable; `Consumers: xtask/tests/policy.rs` with that deliverable; a path under a deliverable directory ending in '/'; a Consumers line naming a non-deliverable and saying 'unchanged'; `Consumers: none found, searched the repo for athena.toml reads`. Unaffected (None): the same deliverables with a criterion that is not a limit; a limit with docs/x.md and no config deliverable; defaults.toml covered by the same cases.
demonstrations.observes: The config reading is refused until every named consumer path is a deliverable or the line says unchanged or none found; readings without a limit or without a config deliverable return None.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the config half the first assertion returns None and the test fails; a rule that accepted any test deliverable fails the 'unrelated test deliverable' assertion; a crates/-only parser fails the xtask assertions; a rule that fired without a limit fails the 'not a limit' assertion.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `refusing_check` through `gate_refuser`, and `check_scope_limit` directly. Fixture: in-memory `Reading`; no double. The seam exists today; step 2 adds the check and step 8 the tests.

demonstrations.method: Step 4 adds `scope_limit_cases()` to `cases()` in crates/athena-core/tests/refusal_corpus.rs, built with the existing `case(..)` helper from `base_reading` with one field changed each (harness `run(&Case)` at refusal_corpus.rs:2189 and the wrapper test at 2220). Refuse("check_scope_limit"), 9 cases: 'only X may change' with a dash bullet, shape of 9bw7's scope (`scope-limit-only-may-change-omits-changelog`); 'no file outside X changed' with a star bullet (`scope-limit-no-file-outside-omits-changelog`); a `1.` numbered request (`scope-limit-numbered-part-omits-changelog`); 'test-only change' naming no file (`scope-limit-test-only-change-omits-changelog`); 'only the docs may change' (`scope-limit-only-the-docs-omits-changelog`); a limit that names CHANGELOG.md and forbids it (`scope-limit-names-changelog-but-forbids-it`); a config deliverable with a limit and no Consumers line, shape of 7z81 (`scope-limit-config-deliverable-without-consumers`); a Consumers line naming a non-deliverable crates/ path (`scope-limit-consumer-not-a-deliverable`); a Consumers line naming a non-deliverable xtask/ path (`scope-limit-xtask-consumer-not-a-deliverable`). Accept, 9 cases: bare 'No other file is changed' (`scope-limit-bare-no-other-file`); 'production unchanged' (`scope-limit-bare-production-unchanged`); a limit naming CHANGELOG.md (`scope-limit-names-changelog`); a limit pointing to the deliverables (`scope-limit-points-to-deliverables`); config deliverable with Consumers paths that are deliverables (`scope-limit-config-consumers-are-deliverables`); with an xtask/ deliverable consumer (`scope-limit-xtask-consumer-is-a-deliverable`); with 'unchanged' (`scope-limit-config-consumers-unchanged`); with 'none found' (`scope-limit-config-consumers-none-found`); a config deliverable with no limit (`config-deliverable-without-a-limit`). New `INPUT_FORMS` tags: `scope-limit-omits-default-file`, `scope-limit-forbids-default-file`, `scope-limit-config-without-consumers`, `scope-limit-names-default-file`, `scope-limit-consumer-not-a-deliverable`; the array length is updated. athena.toml and the consumer paths go in the cases' `repo_files` so the later boundary check passes. I read the corpus layout (existing cases such as `code-reading-without-a-survey`, `criterion-rests-on-the-producer-report`) but saw no test result; the producer and verifier run the command.

open_questions: User: crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs (LIMIT constant, forced) and crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs (one test) are outside the six deliverables of the accepted reading. If the verification scope guard treats the deliverable list as an allowlist for this job, please add both files to the reading's deliverables; otherwise the plan keeps them as minimal edits under the request's crates/ scope.

User: criterion 3 says a reading with an athena.toml deliverable and a limit passes by adding 'a crates/ test deliverable' or a `Consumers:` assumption. This plan shows it in a revised sense: it passes only when every consumer path named in the Consumers line is a deliverable, or the line says unchanged or none found. A bare test deliverable with no Consumers line stays refused, because that left 7z81's failure open (the tests were listed or not at random, and nothing tied them to the config). Also, a Consumers line that only says it searched, with no path and no 'none found', is refused. D166 records both. Say if you want the literal wording instead.

User: the accepted reading says a scope limit may also be an out_of_scope item, and that listing CHANGELOG.md as a deliverable is enough. The code settles both: verification reads criteria only (briefs.rs:103-108), and the gate always sees the CHANGELOG.md deliverable because ensure_changelog runs first (reading.rs:859). This plan checks criteria only and requires the limit text to name CHANGELOG.md (not negated) or the deliverables, or to be bare. Criterion 2's 'with CHANGELOG.md listed' is shown as the limit naming it.

Host: the share of past accepted readings newly refused cannot be measured from the plan copy, which has no records/. The 3% figure is an estimate, and the round 2 and 3 triggers may raise it; the loop replay at the producer and verifier measures it, and the hold is above 8%.
